display.purpose: Hero headings and track titles at full scale. Maximum one per screen.

headline.purpose: Page titles on both B2C and B2B surfaces, primary section headers.

title.purpose: Card headings, panel section labels, dialog titles.

body.purpose: Prose and descriptions. Max 65–75ch line length.

label.purpose: Navigation items, button text, input labels, metadata, chip text. Legible at 13px due to Space Grotesk's generous x-height.

data.purpose: All numeric API values: play counts, popularity scores, durations, timestamps. Register-locked to data contexts.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Focus ring for primary buttons and focused form inputs. Keyboard navigation only — never on mouse events.

shadows.name: modal-veil
shadows.purpose: Below modal dialogs only. Creates floating separation from the page.

shadows.name: playing-indicator
shadows.purpose: Left-side state indicator for currently-playing track rows and selected B2B analytics rows. Use box-shadow inset — not border-left.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (150ms). Button hover, row hover, nav item color changes.

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: Exiting elements — dropdowns closing, toasts dismissing (100ms).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Analytics row hover, B2B surface transitions. Analysts are scanning; don't slow them down.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Button hover, B2C row hover, nav state changes. The default.

motion.name: duration-deliberate
motion.purpose: Modal open/close, drawer slide-in, player progress-bar scrubbing. Reserved for deliberate UI moments.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tablet portrait — sidebar collapses to bottom nav on B2C

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: Wide desktop — B2B analytics can run multi-panel

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main CTA. Violet fill with pale ink text. Text sized to WCAG large-text threshold (bold ≥14px) for contrast compliance on medium-L violet fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: oklch(0.48 0.15 290); color: oklch(0.92 0.008 285); font-family: 'Space Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 8px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.54 0.16 290); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px oklch(0.48 0.15 290 / 0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.38; cursor: not-allowed; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn-primary { transition: none; } }

components.css: .ds-player { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 12px 24px; background: oklch(0.11 0.011 285); } .ds-player__track { flex: 1; min-width: 0; } .ds-player__title { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 600; color: oklch(0.92 0.008 285); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-player__artist { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 400; color: oklch(0.58 0.010 285); } .ds-player__controls { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-player__btn { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 50%; background: oklch(0.48 0.15 290); color: oklch(0.92 0.008 285); border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-player__btn:hover { background: oklch(0.54 0.16 290); } .ds-player__progress { flex: 2; } .ds-player__bar { height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: oklch(0.25 0.012 285); position: relative; } .ds-player__fill { height: 100%; border-radius: 2px; background: oklch(0.48 0.15 290); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-player__btn { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
A mixing engineer's control room at midnight: every surface earns its presence, the dark field makes the signal glow, and nothing decorates what isn't functional. Tracklytics is not a music app with a dashboard bolted on — it is a platform where listener behavior becomes industry intelligence, and the interface is the conduit between those two registers. The reference points are Figma (deep dark, violet-tinted, precision tool) and Apple Music (immersive dark, editorial, album art as content). Neither is imitated; both inform.

The dark surface is not a stylistic choice — it is the physical environment that makes the signal legible. Album art on near-black, a violet playhead advancing through a waveform, a data trend glowing teal against deep space: these are signal, not decoration.

Two registers, one system. The design vocabulary is shared (spacing, radius, typography, motion), but its expression diverges. B2C: generous padding, cover art as content, violet as immersion. B2B: dense tables, mono data values, teal for positive signal. Neither register apologizes for its register.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-native: surfaces at L 0.09–0.18 in OKLCH, never light-mode defaults with dark paint applied
Dual-register: B2C and B2B surfaces share one token system but express it categorically differently
Signal-forward: color, hierarchy, and space guide the eye to what matters; nothing else gets color
Typography as register: Space Grotesk signals B2C personality, JetBrains Mono signals B2B data authority
Tonal elevation: depth expressed through lightness steps, not shadows
Earned violet: the primary accent appears on ≤15% of any screen; its rarity is the point

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Twilight Violet appears on ≤15% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. When violet is everywhere, the signal disappears.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal carries data meaning. It appears on charts, trend badges, and live-state indicators — never on navigation, headings, or UI chrome.

rules.name: The Mono Gate Rule
rules.body: If a number comes from the API, it is a data value and renders in JetBrains Mono. The question: 'could this number change?' Yes → mono.

rules.name: The Tonal Ladder Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a fourth surface color between the three tonal steps. Ground → Raised → Lifted. Add tonal contrast before adding shadows.

rules.name: The Shadow Prohibition
rules.body: Drop shadows are banned in the dark theme as ambient or decorative elements. Shadows appear only as focus rings and modal veils.

dos: Do use JetBrains Mono for every numeric API value — play counts, popularity scores, durations, engagement metrics
Do use tonal elevation (three lightness steps) to convey surface depth: Ground → Raised → Lifted
Do verify Muted Ink (oklch(0.58 0.010 285)) at ≥4.5:1 against every surface it appears on
Do use Violet Light (oklch(0.68 0.14 290)) for violet text on dark backgrounds — not the primary fill violet
Do keep Twilight Violet on ≤15% of any screen surface
Do add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to every transition and animation
Do maintain 44×44px minimum touch targets for player controls and nav items
Do use box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 <color> for playing/selected row indicators — never border-left
donts: Don't use cheap startup template patterns: identical card grids, eyebrow labels on every section, stock gradient hero fills
Don't build generic dark SaaS — dark theme as a badge, not a design decision
Don't reference Spotify's 2024 aesthetic: oversaturated album-art color splashes, heavy green as primary accent
Don't build bloated enterprise analytics: cluttered sidebars, tiny font, gray-on-gray data tables
Don't use Signal Teal on navigation, decorative highlights, hover backgrounds, or button fills
Don't allow Muted Ink to drop below 4.5:1 contrast on its surface
Don't add drop shadows in the dark theme as ambient depth — use tonal elevation
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe
Don't use Space Grotesk on B2B analytics surfaces
Don't use modal dialogs as first choice for B2B data actions
Don't add gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient fill)
